key_points.point: Top-performing enterprises achieve massive output multiplication through intensive agentic AI adoption, as demonstrated by the finding that frontier firms generate 8.3 times as many output tokens per active user as typical firms. This empirical metric reflects both greater depth of use and the broader integration of agents connected to company context, tools, and repeatable workflows across industries and company sizes. From an accelerationist perspective, this productivity multiplier validates the rapid commercial deployment of agentic systems as a core driver of net economic value and enterprise efficiency. The document notes that access alone is insufficient, requiring complementary organizational investments in employee learning, data infrastructure, and shared workflows to fully capture these gains.
key_points.verbatim: Frontier firms—those in the top 10% of AI usage each month—now generate 8.3 × as many output tokens per active user as typical firms. The measure is a proxy for depth of use, and the widening gap appears alongside greater adoption of capabilities that connect agents to company context, tools, and repeatable workflows.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Frontier firms achieve massive output multiplication through intensive agentic AI adoption.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that top-performing enterprises achieve massive output multiplication through intensive agentic AI adoption, scaling output tokens per active user far beyond typical firms. Encompasses: frontier firm productivity multipliers, token generation multiples, high-usage enterprise cohorts.

key_points.point: Enterprise AI adoption is systematically expanding from mere assistance to autonomous execution, with agentic tools like Codex generating 64 percent of combined output tokens among enterprise customers by June. This shift enables workers to delegate multi-step, complex tasks such as gathering information and drafting presentations directly to AI agents. From an accelerationist viewpoint, this transition represents a fundamental breakthrough in efficiency, turning AI into an engine for widespread economic expansion and cost reduction. The report notes that this shift spans diverse knowledge-work functions, including legal, sales, recruiting, and marketing, rather than remaining confined to software engineering.
key_points.verbatim: As of June, Codex generated 64% of combined Codex and ChatGPT output tokens among enterprise customers, suggesting that agents are enabling a shift toward more substantive, delegated work.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI drives net economic expansion through agentic execution and task delegation.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that AI drives net economic expansion through cost deflation and value creation as agents shift from question-answering to executing multi-step workflows. Encompasses: marginal cost reduction, agentic task delegation, enterprise token generation shifts.

key_points.point: Organizations can scale expert performance and narrow the frontier gap by turning successful individual use cases into repeatable practices across the entire enterprise. The methodology involves identifying employees with the strongest AI habits—often early-career workers who send 13 more messages per week than executives—and making their workflows visible. From an accelerationist perspective, this practice propagation accelerates organizational learning and ensures that cutting-edge productivity gains diffuse rapidly throughout the economy. The document cautions that achieving this requires complementary investments in continuous employee learning, shared workflows, and data infrastructure rather than mere software access.
key_points.verbatim: The opportunity for leaders is to close the frontier gap by extending agentic workflows beyond engineering and turning successful individual use cases into repeatable practices across the organization.
key_points.excerpt_context: What leaders can do to narrow the frontier gap
key_points.canonical_proposition: Scale expert performance across organizations by turning successful individual AI workflows into repeatable practices.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that champions AI's ability to learn from top-performing workers and scale their expert behaviors across an entire organization by propagating effective individual workflows. Encompasses: scaling expert performance, workflow diffusion, early-career AI adoption habits.

key_points.point: Organizations must treat AI deployment as a comprehensive organizational change management challenge rather than a purely technical rollout, establishing clear permissions, governance, and human review frameworks. The strategic approach relies on bundling capabilities with plugins and repeatable instructions while maintaining structured oversight over agentic execution. From a safetyist perspective, this structural governance is essential to maintain operational visibility and control as enterprises transition from passive assistance to autonomous execution. The document notes that access alone is insufficient, requiring robust institutional frameworks and continuous employee support to manage the transition safely.
key_points.verbatim: Together, the studies point to a practical enterprise agenda: connect agents to the context and tools needed to complete valuable work; establish clear permissions, review, and governance; and help employees turn effective individual workflows into shared ways of working.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Treat AI deployment as change management by establishing clear permissions, review, and governance structures.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that views AI adoption primarily as a process of organizational change management rather than a purely technical implementation, incorporating clear permissions, governance, and human review. Encompasses: change management strategies, institutional governance structures, human review frameworks.

key_points.point: AI adoption is reshaping work across multiple knowledge-work functions rather than remaining confined to software engineering, with weekly active enterprise Codex users growing significantly in legal, sales, recruiting, and marketing. The empirical evidence shows that weekly active Codex users surged by 108 percent in legal, 41 percent in sales, 41 percent in recruiting, and 26 percent in marketing over a multi-month period. From a skeptic perspective, this broad functional diffusion demonstrates that AI restructuring impacts professional white-collar labor markets unevenly and rapidly across sectors. The document notes that engineering was merely an early center of adoption, whereas the current wave alters diverse occupational workflows.
key_points.verbatim: Software engineering was an early center of agentic adoption, but Codex use is now growing quickly across knowledge-work functions. Since February, weekly active enterprise Codex users grew 108 % in legal, 41 % in sales, 41 % in recruiting, and 26 % in marketing, compared with 5 % in engineering.
key_points.excerpt_context: Agents are spreading across knowledge work
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI is reshaping work across multiple professional domains, driving rapid adoption in legal, sales, recruiting, and marketing.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that examines the multifaceted ways AI is changing the job market and worker experience across diverse professional domains like legal, sales, recruiting, and marketing. Encompasses: knowledge-work functional restructuring, cross-sector adoption growth, white-collar labor impact.

As of June, Codex generated 64% of combined Codex and ChatGPT output tokens among OpenAI enterprise customers.
Weekly active users of Plugins represent 21% at frontier firms compared to 9% at typical firms, while 95% of active employees at OpenAI use Plugins weekly.
Since February, weekly active enterprise Codex users grew 108% in legal, 41% in sales, 41% in recruiting, and 26% in marketing, compared with 5% in engineering.
Six months after enterprise adoption, early-career employees sent 13 more messages per week on average than executives.
